title: Smooth-proper purity of the constant Weil sheaf
statement:
Fix the global finite-field datum
$(p,a,q,k_0,k)$, where $p$ is prime and $a\in\mathbf Z_{\geq1}$ with
$q=p^a$. Choose a prime $\ell\neq p$, an algebraic closure
$\Qlb$ of $\Ql=\mathbf Q_\ell$, and an isomorphism
$\iota:\Qlb\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathbf C$. Interpret the $\Qlb$-objects
in the algebraically
closed coefficient category. Let
$X_0/k_0$ be smooth, proper,
geometrically connected of pure dimension
$d\in\mathbf Z_{\geq0}$, and put $X=X_0\times_{k_0}k$. Let
$a_X:X\to\Spec k$ be the structure morphism, and let
$g_X=\operatorname{id}_{X_0}\times\operatorname{Spec}(\operatorname{Frob}_q)$
be the geometric-Frobenius automorphism.
Let $F_\ell$ be the induced
global geometric Frobenius
on the ordinary and
compactly supported cohomology with $\Ql$-coefficients,
and let $F_{\Qlb}$ be its scalar extension to the corresponding
$\Qlb$-cohomology. Define the graded cohomology notation by

$$
H^\bullet(X,\Lambda):=\bigoplus_{i\in\mathbf Z}H^i(X,\Lambda),
\qquad
H_c^\bullet(X,\Lambda):=\bigoplus_{i\in\mathbf Z}H_c^i(X,\Lambda)
\quad(\Lambda=\Ql,\Qlb).
$$

Use the scalar-extension identifications

$$
H^\bullet(X,\Ql)\otimes_{\Ql}\Qlb\simeq H^\bullet(X,\Qlb),\qquad
H_c^\bullet(X,\Ql)\otimes_{\Ql}\Qlb\simeq H_c^\bullet(X,\Qlb).
$$

Assume $a_X:X\to\Spec k$ is
exceptional-adjoint
admissible at $\Qlb$, and choose a dualizing
Weil complex
$(\omega_X,\theta_{\omega_X})$ with

$$
\operatorname{For}(\omega_X)=Ra_X^!\Qlb,
$$

where $Ra_X^!$ is the
exceptional inverse image
for this admissible structure morphism, and require
$\theta_{\omega_X}$ to be the canonical functorial Weil lift induced by
geometric-Frobenius base change and the adjunction units and counits, rather
than an arbitrary lift.
These operators come from the constant
Weil sheaf $(\Qlb)_X$ on the
small pro-etale site, with the
geometric-Frobenius convention. Fix an
indeterminate $T$. For
$0\leq i\leq2d$, set

$$
H^i(X,\Qlb)=H^i\!\left(R\Gamma(X,(\Qlb)_X)\right),\qquad
H_c^i(X,\Qlb)=H^i\!\left(R\Gamma_c(X,(\Qlb)_X)\right),
\qquad
V_{i,\ell}=H^i(X,\Ql),
$$

and $F_{i,\ell}=F_\ell|_{V_{i,\ell}}$,
$P_{i,\ell}(T)=\det(1-TF_{i,\ell}\mid V_{i,\ell})$. These data are the
smooth-proper
cohomological family; reciprocal roots use the
ordinary/reciprocal-root
convention. Use the
complex-weight and
Frobenius-module weight
predicates. Then the constant
Weil sheaf $(\Qlb)_X$ is
$\iota$-pure of weight $0$.

proof.text: Use exactly the finite-field datum $(p,a,q,k_0,k)$, the prime $\ell\neq p$, the coefficient field $\Qlb$ in the algebraically closed coefficient category, the smooth proper geometrically connected $X_0$ of pure dimension $d$, the geometric fibre $X$ and the structure morphism $a_X$ fixed in the statement. Clause (3) of [lem-weil-smooth-proper-purity-hypotheses] applies to these data and shows that for every integer $j$ the groups $H^j(X,\Qlb)$ and $H_c^j(X,\Qlb)$ of [def-weil-ordinary-compact-cohomology] are finite-dimensional $\Qlb$-vector spaces carrying the action of the global geometric Frobenius. This discharges the explicit finiteness hypothesis of [thm-weil-deligne-purity] used in Step 2; no hypothesis is added to the item.

source.place: proof paragraph: 'whose hypotheses are exactly the smoothness, properness, geometric connectedness, coefficient, and Frobenius data fixed above'

proof.text: Apply [thm-weil-deligne-purity] with $i=0$ (allowed since $d\geq0$) to the same $p,a,q,k_0,k,\ell,\Qlb,\iota,X_0,X,d,a_X,g_X$. Its smoothness, properness, geometric connectedness and pure-dimension hypotheses are those of the statement; the exceptional-adjoint admissibility of $a_X$ at $\Qlb$ and the dualizing Weil complex $(\omega_X,\theta_{\omega_X})$ with $\operatorname{For}(\omega_X)=Ra_X^!\Qlb$ and canonical functorial Weil lift are assumed in the statement verbatim; the finiteness of the displayed cohomology groups is Step 1. The theorem's cohomology $H^i(Ra_{X*}(\Qlb)_X)$, $H^i(Ra_{X!}(\Qlb)_X)$ is the item's $H^i(R\Gamma(X,(\Qlb)_X))$, $H^i(R\Gamma_c(X,(\Qlb)_X))$ by the definition $R\Gamma=\operatorname{Fib}_s\circ Ra_{X*}$, $R\Gamma_c=\operatorname{Fib}_s\circ Ra_{X!}$ of [def-weil-ordinary-compact-cohomology], and both statements use the same constant $\Qlb$-Weil object on the small pro-etale site of [def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex]. Its weight predicate for $(\Qlb)_X$ is the one of [def-weil-complex-weights], formed with the same chosen $\omega_X$: the upper predicate on the cohomology sheaves and the lower one through $D_X$. Assertion (1) of the theorem then says that $(\Qlb)_X$ is $\iota$-pure of weight $0$, which is the conclusion.
